item.title: Photos: A Deadly Flood Tears Through Nepal and Tibet
item.description: An ice avalanche that started high in the Himalayas tumbled thousands of feet, releasing vast amounts of energy that pulverized the ice into a significant volume of flood water.
item.dc:creator: The New York Times

item.title: Trump’s Strength in Primaries is Clear. The Midterms Pose a Different Test.
item.description: The president’s pull with the party base has been clear and his resources are vast. But his low approval ratings make him a liability with swing voters.

item.media:credit: Bryan Anselm for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump campaigning with Representative Mike Lawler of New York in May. Republicans have to weigh Mr. Trump’s approval ratings against his popularity among his base.

item.title: Yayoi Kusama, Japanese Pop Artist Known for Polka-Dot Paintings, Dies at 97
item.description: The Japanese artist’s polka-dot-covered paintings, phallic sculptures and public performances caused a stir in New York City and Europe in the 1960s.
item.dc:creator: Holland Cotter

item.title: Yayoi Kusama Was the Avant-Garde Radical Who Became a Pop Icon
item.description: In her mass-produced ubiquity, Kusama became one of her own dots, spreading her image into every corner of our culture.
item.dc:creator: Blake Gopnik
item.media:description: A video projection of “Song of a Manhattan Suicide Addict,” by Yayoi Kusama, in 2024. In her later years, Kusama was one of the most popular living artists in the world.

item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Wants to Make Sure YouTube and TikTok Share His Pain
item.description: Meta, the social media giant, agreed to change the way children interact with its apps. That could be trouble if its competitors don’t abide by the same rules.
item.dc:creator: Mike Isaac
item.media:description: To settle the suits, Meta agreed to drastically rein in children’s’ access to marquee products like Instagram and Facebook.

item.title: A Movement to Restrict Social Media for Children Has Taken Hold Globally
item.description: Governments around the world have passed or proposed a range of bans or restrictions on young teens using addictive social media platforms.
item.dc:creator: Ephrat Livni
item.media:description: A 15-year-old using social media apps in Australia in July, more than half a year after the country had implemented a ban on children under 16 using many platforms.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Appears to Be Preparing for a New War With the Houthis
item.description: Analysts say that weeks of Houthi attacks on Saudi targets have brought the kingdom and the Iranian-backed militia to the brink of full-blown conflict, and could open a new front in the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Vivian Nereim
item.media:description: A demonstration in Sanaa, Yemen’s capital, in support of the Houthi militia last month. The Houthis, who control northern Yemen on Saudi Arabia’s southern border, are supported by Iran.
